title: Hampton University (Hampton)
summary: Hampton University (Hampton) is a university in Hampton. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with Hampton.

sections.heading: What Hampton is known for
paragraphs: Hampton University, a private nonprofit institution, is recognized for its diverse academic offerings and commitment to student success. With an undergraduate enrollment of 3,727 students, Hampton provides a range of programs that cater to various interests and career goals. Notably, about 20.2% of its programs focus on business, reflecting a strong emphasis on preparing students for the corporate world. Additionally, health-related programs constitute approximately 10.51% of the academic offerings, highlighting Hampton's dedication to the growing healthcare sector. The university maintains an admission rate of 62.25%, indicating a moderately selective admissions process. Overall, Hampton is known for balancing a broad educational experience with specialized programs in business and health.

sections.heading: How to read Hampton tuition
paragraphs: Hampton University charges the same tuition rate for both in-state and out-of-state students, which is $30,592. This uniform tuition policy simplifies the cost structure for all students regardless of their residency status. However, the total cost of attendance at Hampton is higher than tuition alone, amounting to $46,027. This figure includes additional expenses such as fees, room and board, books, and other personal costs that students should consider when planning their finances.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: Financial aid plays a significant role at Hampton University, with approximately 39.35% of students receiving Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies aimed at supporting low-income undergraduates. For students who complete their programs, the median debt upon graduation is $25,442, reflecting the typical borrowing amount required to finance their education. Prospective and current students can explore detailed financial aid information and use the net price calculator available on Hampton's official website at www.hamptonu.edu/. Additional data on costs and aid can also be accessed through the U.S. Department of Education's College Scorecard at https://collegescorecard.ed.gov/school/?232265.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: Career outcomes for Hampton University (Hampton) students show varied results in earnings and debt. The completion rate within 150% of the normal time is approximately 57.16%, indicating that just over half of students finish their programs within this timeframe. Median earnings for graduates six years after entry are $42,721, while median earnings ten years after entry increase to $59,159, reflecting growth in income as alumni advance in their careers. For those who complete their programs, the median debt upon graduation is $25,442, representing the typical amount borrowed to finance their education. These figures provide insight into the financial and professional trajectories of Hampton students following their studies.
